QuestionStmt.S: Select the incorrect statement about $N_2$ molecule.

Option1Stmt.S: It is more stable than $O_2$ molecule.

Option2Stmt.S: It consists more electrons in bonding molecular orbitals than $O_2$.

Solution.S:
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}
\hline
\text{Molecule} & \text{No. of electrons in bonding MOs} & \text{Bond order} & \text{Magnetic nature} \\
\hline
N_2 & 10 & 3 & \text{Diamagnetic} \\
O_2 & 10 & 2 & \text{Paramagnetic} \\
\hline
\end{array}$$

Both $N_2$ and $O_2$ have 10 electrons in bonding molecular orbitals. So statement B is incorrect because it claims $N_2$ has more bonding electrons than $O_2$; they are equal. Hence the correct option is B.
